title: Explainable artificial intelligence as AI literacy scaffolding
abstract:
This conceptual paper responds to the growing gap in artificial intelligence (AI) literacy among users of large language models (LLMs) and other AI systems in recent years. While explainable AI (XAI) has largely been framed as a mechanism for transparency and accountability, its potential to be used as a developmental learning support for end users remains underexplored. The purpose of this article is to conceptualize explainability as a form of literacy scaffolding that supports the gradual, in situ development of AI literacy skills through explanation-driven interaction.
 
 
 
 A conceptual framework is developed through an integrative analysis of literature from explainable AI, AI literacy, educational scaffolding theory and human–AI teaming research. Key concepts are defined, and theoretical parallels are drawn between scaffolding processes in education and explanation-driven interaction with AI systems.
 
 
 
 We argue that AI explanations can function as a scaffold that supports users in learning not only about specific outputs but also about model behavior, limitations, and potential bias. This framework is organized around three core scaffolding principles: the contingent support calibrated to the learner's Zone of Proximal Development, progressive fading of explanatory support as competence grows, and the reframing of explanations as entry points for inquiry rather than disclosure endpoints. These principles collectively support the development of calibrated trust among users rather than uncritical acceptance or unwarranted skepticism toward AI models.
 
 
 
 This article offers a theoretical framework for understanding explainability as AI literacy scaffolding and outlines implications for the design and evaluation of XAI systems. It further proposes methodological approaches for empirically identifying and measuring scaffolding behavior in user interactions with XAI. By positioning explainability as a mechanism for fostering durable AI literacy and calibrated trust, this work contributes to information science scholarship on human–AI interaction and responsible AI use.

title: Who to activate next? Predicting influential and susceptible users in social media marketing with CFT-SIS
abstract:
The proliferation of online social networks (OSNs) has brought opportunities and challenges in managing marketing information flows. This study aims to develop an organization-level personalized monitoring model for marketing campaigns, which not only tracks the dynamics of information dissemination but also identifies influential, susceptible and cost-efficient participants to activate in the next round of campaigns.
 
 
 
 This study develops a novel CFT-SIS framework that integrates curated flows theory (CFT) with the epidemiological susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) framework and differentiates information dissemination through broadcasting and narrowcasting channels. It combines users’ susceptibility with their historical influence in brand-specific campaigns to construct the influence-susceptibility index (ISI), precisely measuring both activation difficulty and resulting impact.
 
 
 
 The CFT-SIS framework enables real-time monitoring of information diffusion by capturing both horizontal spread within individual campaigns and longitudinal interconnections across multiple campaigns. Compared to conventional SIS formulations, it demonstrates higher accuracy and stability in predicting user states. The proposed ISI effectively identifies dual-role users who are both highly influential and easily activated, enabling deeper propagation at lower cost and highlighting participants who drive sustained campaign success.
 
 
 
 This study advances theoretical understanding of sustained social media marketing by identifying a novel and structurally emergent mechanism through which curation hierarchy reshapes user susceptibility and influence across network positions over time. In practice, the model enables the identification of high-impact, easily activated users, supporting more efficient campaign design and resource allocation in social media marketing.
